page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 compute instance configured with a dedicated 4 vCPU allocation backed by 2 physical Intel cores and 2 threads per core. Equipped with 32 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 260 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and provisioned instances do not feature local GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluation shows a clear split between single-threaded efficiency and overall multi-core scale. Single-core performance lands squarely in the mid-range tier, producing 1,564.68 on stress-ng and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,868.0, with web serving throughput reaching 7.0 GB/sec and small model (135M) LLM text generation hitting 92.48 tokens per second. In contrast, total multi-core execution falls into the lower 25th percentile, reflected by a multi-core Geekbench score of 4,154.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5,956.49, constrained by the modest 4 vCPU baseline. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 33.17 GB/sec, while Redis SET throughput reaches 4.93 million operations per second.

From an operational and resource efficiency standpoint, the instance offers dense memory capacity without incurring the expense of higher core counts. The inclusion of AMX matrix acceleration and AVX-512 provides tailored instruction-level speedups for supported tasks despite low aggregate core parallelism. Workloads suited for the n4-highmem-4 include medium-scale in-memory caches, memory-bound database engines, lightweight ETL workflows, and intermediate application servers requiring high RAM headroom with standard computational throughput.
